name: Posterior cruciate ligament
description: From the medial femoral condyle in the notch to the posterior intercondylar tibia below the joint line, thicker than the ACL. Uniformly low signal and unstriated, a smooth arc usually seen whole on one sagittal slice.

normal_values.ap_diameter_vertical_portion: under 7 mm on sagittal; 7 mm or more strongly suggests a tear
normal_values.pcl_angle: below about 107–115° (buckled) supports an ACL tear; hyperextension can also buckle it

variants_pitfalls: Magic angle can make the proximal curve intermediate on short-TE images, and tears can be brighter on PD than T2, so let thickness, continuity and edema decide, not signal.

Double PCL sign: a second low-signal band just anteroinferior to the PCL is a displaced bucket-handle fragment, usually medial. A ligament of Humphry sits there too but is thin (about 1.5–2 mm) and traces to the lateral meniscus; confirm a fragment with an absent bow tie and a truncated meniscus.
Meniscofemoral ligaments (at least one in about 91–93% of cadaver knees) can mimic a loose body; trace them to the lateral meniscus.
Tears usually stay in continuity, as a thickened PCL with intermediate signal; chronic tears can heal lax and near normal. A fibular styloid avulsion (arcuate sign) should prompt a close look.
